set.approach: From the Crest Lake parking area, cross the highway and follow the trail east to the Crow's Nest, then go around the corner to the right and up the hill into the alcove. Climb the crack along the right edge of the staging platform.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at the top.

set.approach: The trailhead is at the head of Powell Lake and needs a boat transfer. From there bike up the Daniels valley beside the Daniels River, then bushwhack up to the subalpine on the east ridge. Cross a few bumps to a final bump on the ridge, which is descended on its left side by slippery fourth class, and the east face is then in view; campsites lie on the way to the base of the steep rock.
set.descent_text: Downclimb or rappel the route ledge to ledge in short rappels.

set.approach: From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the foot of the south face. The route is on the southwest side of the peak, and the first two pitches can be skipped by using the SW spur from the Dione couloir.

set.approach: From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the base of the peak. The route is on the west side of Dione.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Reach the south face of Dione from the hut by crossing the glacier. At the south face, drop well down to an obvious col on your right, pass through it, descend snow then ascend again to the foot of the steep snow couloir serving several west-face lines.
set.descent_text: From just south of the summit, rappel the normal route down the east side from fixed cord to bolted rap stations, onto the snowfield capping Petite Dione. Cross the top of Petite Dione heading south, downclimb, and reach the head of Le Petit Couloir, where bolted rappels lead to the ground.

set.approach: From the hut, go to Red Tit Col, then follow the broad Dione Glacier across the west flank under the peak's extended south ridge. The hut gives a clear view of the line. Crossing the moat to reach the rock can be hard in mid to late season. The route begins with the lower pitches of Dehydrated on Dalwhinnie, or climbs from the couloir approach to a two-bolt belay at the top of a blocky gully.
set.descent_text: Scramble along the ridge to the summit ledge of Dione, then downclimb or rappel the southeast face.

set.approach: From the hut, cross the Dione Glacier to the foot of the south face. The route begins from the Dione couloir, where an easy fourth class ramp leads onto the rock on the southwest side of the peak.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: Follow the Drinnan Pass trail from the trailhead to a large open talus field and cross it below Drinnan Slab. On the far side a seasonal stream crosses the trail right under the slab's lowest point; scramble up and right below the cliff to the foot of Slabadabadoo, then continue up and right along the gully at the slab's base. The route starts on a low-angle grassy ledge below an overhanging arch system.
set.descent_text: Walking off is easy and preferred. Start on the level grassy bench over the slab and head north toward Drinnan Lake and take the narrower right-hand (east) gully of the two parallel ones; the west gully cliffs out. Cross the talus field, follow open glades to the lake, and take the Drinnan Pass trail down. The route can also be rappelled with two ropes.

set.approach: Follow the Drinnan Pass trail from the trailhead to a large open talus field and cross it below Drinnan Slab. On the far side a seasonal stream crosses the trail right under the slab's lowest point; scramble up and to the left from there. The climb begins on a broad, sloping ledge slightly above the slab's bottom edge and follows a vertical line up the centre, just left of a dark water streak.
set.descent_text: Walking off is easy. Start on the level grassy bench over the slab and head north toward Drinnan Lake and take the narrower right-hand (east) gully of the two parallel ones; the west gully cliffs out. Cross the talus field, follow open glades to the lake, and take the Drinnan Pass trail down. The route can also be rappelled with two ropes.

set.approach: Drive the Bannock forest road toward Gimli. From the Gimli base camp, head east toward a small peak, aim for the horizontal ridgeline running south from it, and cross over by way of a talus gully into the basin below Wolfs Ears. From the foot of the west ear, traverse east to the deep gully between the two ears. A shallow cave to the right of the gully marks the start of the first pitch.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route on single ropes back to its base. Some rappels use nearly a full rope, so knot the rope ends, and on the fifth pitch rappel on the outside of the chockstone.

set.approach: The easiest way into Frontier Creek is a charter flight. From a camp on the col southeast of the ridgeline, traverse onto the southwest side, working up and down gullies and along benches to a gully that joins a rock shoulder beneath the third sub-peak. The approach is loose and tiring; the route then climbs that shoulder.
set.descent_text: From the summit area, downclimb to the second sub-peak and make a single rappel to the notch between the third and second sub-peaks. Scramble down a loose gully and return by the line of approach.

set.approach: The easiest way into Frontier Creek is a charter flight. Trident Tower lies just southeast of Diana Mountain. Scramble up the gullies and bench system southwest of the summit to the foot of the large face; the route follows a chimney that holds a big chockstone.
set.descent_text: Make a short down-lead from the summit, then rappel the route to its base. A tag line is useful because the first pitch offers no place for an intermediate anchor.

set.approach: From Lake of the Woods in the core of Cathedral Provincial Park, take the Goat Lake trail to the lake. Follow the right shore to its end and contour up rightward through talus and meadows into the larch basin below Macabre Tower. The route is on the tower's north face and starts left of centre, above treeline at the head of a scree and talus slope, on blocky orange rock.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the summit slightly to the skier's left toward the large terrace and gully below. Further rappels lead into the snow and dirt gully, which can be walked down and circled back under the face to the start. Anchors are pins and nuts joined with cord, and may need to be reinforced.

set.approach: From Lake of the Woods in the core of Cathedral Provincial Park, take the Goat Lake trail to the lake. Follow the right shore to its end, then angle left across a gravel fan toward Denture Ridge and climb the steep, crumbly scree and talus slopes southeast of the lake to a buttress on the left, just short of Denture Ridge's crest. The first pitch lies along the buttress's right flank, above a small cone of talus and grass, where a conspicuous crack and dike slants from right to left.
set.descent_text: Hike off.

set.approach: From Lake of the Woods in the core of Cathedral Provincial Park, take the Goat Lake trail to the south end of the lake, then angle left across a gravel fan toward the scree and talus below Denture Ridge and climb to the crest. From the pass, drop down a short way on the far side and traverse left on ledges below the rock wall, continuing down and left to the south side, where the sunny south wall holds the route. Its first pitch leaves an open ledge up a crack.
set.descent_text: The top is a broad grassy flat. Short rappels lead directly back to the pass on Denture Ridge; look for the anchors made of pins, nuts and cord.

set.approach: From the Wall Creek meadow camp, hike directly up the loose slope by goat trails toward the Macabre-Grimface notch until the obvious cleft in the southeast flank of Grimface appears. Climb slabs to the foot of the chimney.
set.descent_text: The usual descent is down the west ridge.

set.approach: From the Wall Creek meadow camp, hike directly up the loose slope by goat trails to the southwest face of Matriarch. The route follows a prominent left-facing corner, with the Lady Fanny of Omaha SW Buttress to its right; rambling pitches lead to the corner.
set.descent_text: Continue along the Matriarch-Macabre-Grimface traverse and come down Grimface's west ridge to return to the meadow.

set.approach: From the Wall Creek meadow camp, hike up the slope by goat trails to the notch southeast of the Grimface summit. The route starts just below the notch, up a chimney with a chockstone near the exit.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the northwest; cairns mark the easiest way down.

set.approach: Take the established Hermit trail up until the cliff shows through the thinning timber, then contour west through several bushy gullies to a level bench on the Grizzly avalanche path. Cross the bench low to the boulder field, ford the creek, and climb to the left side of the small waterfalls above. From the foot of the falls traverse up and left along cairns to the upper boulder field, then cross it to the cliff base. The route is the clean, continuous crack system running up the centre of the face, with a large anchored ledge a short way up that can be reached from the left when snow lingers at the base.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route.

set.approach: Park for the Hermit Meadows trail, hike to the end-of-trail sign and keep going a few hundred metres, then drop down a steep slope into the canyon of the Hermit Narrows and head uphill. Baby Alpine is on the fourth wall up the canyon, the biggest crag.
set.descent_text: After the finish, scramble up and over slabs to an alpine lake, then hike back down into the grassy gully at the foot of the wall.

Crystal Castle is on the right, on the third wall up, which has obvious white quartzite near the top.
set.descent_text: Walk down the ledges on the skier's right into the gully below the Baby Alpine wall.

The route climbs the flakes on the right side of a huge chimney feature, and its belay tree is shared with Screams Across the Valley.

The route is the right-most arete on the second wall, starting on large blocky ground just left of the arete.
